<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2012, 2011 and 2010, the Company paid regular quarterly dividends of&#160;$0.25 per share of Class A for a total of approximately $3,071,000, $3,116,000 and $3,161,000, respectively.&#160;&#160;On November 20, 2012, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors declared a special cash dividend of twenty dollars ($20) per share on its outstanding Class A payable on December 18, 2012 to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 3, 2012.&#160;&#160;The aggregate amount of the special dividend was approximately $61,420,000.&#160;&#160;The Board of Directors also approved a $20 antidilution adjustment reducing the exercise price of all outstanding SARs issued prior to November 20, 2012 to account for the anticipated effect of the special dividend on the Company&#8217;s Class A share price.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Critical Accounting Policies</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP) requires management to make estimates and assumptions about future events that may affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, as well as the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Management has established accounting policies that they believe are appropriate in order to reflect the accurate reporting of the Company&#8217;s operating results, financial position and cash flows.&#160;&#160;The Company applies these accounting policies in a consistent manner.&#160;&#160;Management bases their estimates on historical experience, current and expected economic conditions and various other factors that management believes to be reasonable under the circumstances.&#160;&#160;These estimates and assumptions form the basis for making judgments about various aspects of the Company&#8217;s business, including the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources.&#160;&#160;The Company reevaluates these significant factors and makes adjustments where facts and circumstances dictate.&#160;&#160;Future events and their effects cannot be determined with absolute certainty, and therefore actual results may differ from estimates.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management believes that the following accounting policies are the most critical in the preparation of the Company&#8217;s financial statements because they involve the most difficult, subjective or complex judgments about the effect of matters that are inherently uncertain.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Inventories and Cost of Sales</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Supermarket nonperishable inventories are recorded using the retail method and are stated at the lower of cost or market, with cost determined using the last-in, first-out (LIFO) method.&#160;&#160;Perishable inventories are valued at the lower of cost on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis or market.&#160;&#160;Under the retail inventory method, cost of sales is determined by applying a cost-to-retail ratio to sales for the period to determine cost of sales.&#160;&#160;Cost of sales is then deducted from beginning inventory plus purchases to arrive at ending inventory.&#160;&#160;The Company performs physical inventories of nonperishable items at all of its locations three times per year, at which time ending inventory and cost of sales are adjusted to reflect actual inventory on hand and cost of sales.&#160;&#160;Physical inventories of perishable products are conducted at the end of each fiscal month.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">22</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Approximately 87.5% and 88.0% of the Company&#8217;s inventories were valued using the LIFO method as of December 29, 2012 and December 31, 2011, respectively.&#160;&#160;The LIFO method assumes that the cost of the most recently purchased items are the first to be sold, and thus, are used to measure cost of sales, leaving the earlier costs residing in the ending inventory valuation.&#160;&#160;The Company uses the Link-Chain, Dollar-Value method for purposes of calculating its LIFO charge or credit each year for nonperishable inventories.&#160;&#160;This method requires management to compute a cumulative price index which represents the change in inventory cost since the base year (i.e., the beginning of the year in which LIFO was first elected) compared to the current cost of inventory.&#160;&#160;The cumulative index is then applied to the current cost of inventory to determine the value of inventory at base year costs.&#160;&#160;This computation is performed separately for each of the Company&#8217;s individual LIFO pools (i.e., groupings of similar items such as basic grocery, housewares, alcoholic beverages, etc.).&#160;&#160;The LIFO method requires management to make assumptions and to apply judgment regarding inventory mix and factors related to the computation of price indices which could impact the ending inventory valuation as well as cost of sales.&#160;&#160;If the FIFO method had been used for nonperishable inventories instead of the LIFO method, total inventory as of December 29, 2012 and December 31, 2011 would have been higher by approximately $7,474,000 and $6,897,000, respectively.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company evaluates inventory shortages throughout the year based on actual physical counts at its stores and warehouse.&#160;&#160;Allowances for inventory shortages are recorded based on the results of these counts to provide for estimated shortages from the last physical count to the financial statement date.&#160;&#160;Although the Company has sufficient historical data to record reasonable estimates of inventory shortages, actual results could differ.&#160;&#160;As of December 29, 2012, a difference between actual and estimated shortages of, for example, 25 basis points would have an annual impact of approximately $604,000 on cost of sales.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company monitors the carrying value of long-lived assets for potential impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of an asset may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;Impairment is recognized when estimated future cash flows (undiscounted and before interest charges) are less than carrying value.&#160;&#160;The factor that most significantly affects the impairment calculation is management&#8217;s estimate of future cash flows which is inherently uncertain and relies on various assumptions regarding current and future economic and market conditions and the availability of capital.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s cash flow projection looks several years into the future and includes assumptions such as the rate of inflation/deflation, the strength of the economy, competition in our trade area, the ability to secure subtenants and the Company&#8217;s ability to negotiate early termination agreements.&#160;&#160;If impairment analysis assumptions change, then an adjustment to the carrying value of the Company&#8217;s long-lived assets could occur.&#160;&#160;To the extent that an asset is impaired, the excess of the carrying amount of the asset over its estimated fair value is charged against earnings.&#160;&#160;No asset impairment charges or adjustments were recognized during fiscal 2012, 2011 or 2010.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Workers&#8217; Compensation and General and Auto Liability Insurance</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is primarily self-insured (i) for losses for all years related to general and auto liability claims and (ii) for some years prior to July&#160;1, 2006 for workers&#8217; compensation.&#160;&#160;Where primarily self-insured, the Company purchases stop-loss insurance coverage to limit its loss exposure on a per claim basis.&#160;&#160;Related accruals are based on undeveloped reported claims and an estimate of claims incurred but not reported.&#160;&#160;The amount of reserves for reported claims are determined by a third party administrator claims representative who considers the individual facts of each claim including severity in arriving at an estimate of the Company&#8217;s total exposure.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company analyzes its historical paid and incurred loss trends in order to further develop an estimate of its ultimate cost of undeveloped reported claims and claims incurred but not reported.&#160;&#160;Such estimates and historical trends are not an absolute indication of future results, and the Company reevaluates these reserves quarterly based on the most current information available.&#160;&#160;The ultimate cost of claims are impacted by numerous variables including the frequency and severity of claims, legal and legislative trends, changes in benefit levels, the rate of inflation and claim settlement patterns.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">23</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Since July 1, 2006, the Company has purchased fully insured guaranteed cost workers&#8217; compensation insurance thereby limiting its exposure for workers&#8217; compensation to the cost of the related insurance premium.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s self-insured workers&#8217; compensation accrual for claims incurred prior to July 2006 decreased from $1,585,000 at the beginning of fiscal 2012 to $1,429,000 at the end of the year as a result of payments of $144,000 and reserve adjustments of $12,000.&#160;&#160;The Company expects the workers&#8217; compensation reserve to continue to decline as it continues to pay down and close outstanding workers&#8217; compensation claims which occurred prior to July 1, 2006.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s reserves for general and auto liability claims decreased by approximately $883,000 during fiscal 2012.&#160;&#160;The net decrease reflects payments of $682,000 and a net accrual reversal of $201,000.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Vendor Allowances</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company receives a variety of allowances from its vendors whose products are sold in Gelson&#8217;s stores.&#160;&#160;Typically, the vendors are paying the Company to promote their products.&#160;&#160;The promotion may be a temporary price reduction, a feature in a print advertisement or newsletter, placement of the vendor&#8217;s product in a preferred location in a store or introduction of a new product.&#160;&#160;The promotions range from approximately two weeks to six months and are recognized as a reduction of cost of sales as they are earned.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Vendor funds that have been earned as a result of completing the required performance under the terms of the underlying agreements but for which the product has not yet been sold are recognized as reductions of inventory.&#160;&#160;The amount and timing of recognition of vendor allowances as a reduction of cost of sales, as well as the amount of vendor funds remaining in ending inventory, requires management judgment and estimates.&#160;&#160;Management estimates current year purchase volume based on projected and historical data.&#160;&#160;In turn, the estimated purchase volume is used to determine the amount of vendor allowances to recognize each period.&#160;&#160;The Company does not expect that there will be a significant change in the annual level of vendor support; however, a one percent change in total vendor funds earned would likewise impact gross profit by approximately .03% as a percent of sales.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock Appreciation Rights</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Outstanding SARs are revalued at the end of each quarter using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model which incorporates various highly subjective assumptions, including expected term, expected volatility, expected dividend yield and a risk-free interest rate.&#160;&#160;The fair value of SARs, as determined using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model, does not necessarily reflect the amount that will be paid out in accordance with the SARs agreement on the date of exercise.&#160;&#160;In addition, changes in the market price of the Company&#8217;s Class A can and have significantly impacted the recognition or reversal of SARs expense.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Recent Accounting Standards</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In May 2011, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) 2011-04, &#8220;Amendments to Achieve Common Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure Requirements in U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).&#8221;&#160;&#160;This pronouncement was issued to provide a consistent definition of fair value and ensure that the fair value measurement and disclosure requirements are similar between U.S. GAAP and IFRS.&#160;&#160;ASU 2011-04 changes certain fair value measurement principles and enhances the disclosure requirements particularly for level three fair value measurements.&#160;&#160;This pronouncement is effective for reporting periods beginning on or after December 15, 2011.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASU 2011-04 did not have any impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position or results of operations.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2013, the FASB issued ASU 2013-02, &#8220;Reporting of Amounts Reclassified Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income.&#8221;&#160;&#160;This amendment does not change the current requirements for reporting net income or other comprehensive income in financial statements; however, the amendment requires an entity to provide information about the amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by component and to disclose significant amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by the respective line items of net income if the amount being reclassified is required under U.S.&#160;GAAP to be reclassified in its entirety to net income.&#160;&#160;For other amounts that are not required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in their entirety to net income in the same reporting period, an entity is required to cross-reference other disclosures required under U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;&#160;The pronouncement is effective for reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2012.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASU 2013-02 is not expected to have a significant impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Item 7A.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risks</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company currently has no outstanding bank debt or fixture financing.&#160;&#160;If the Company should borrow in the future, the Company could then be exposed to market risk related to interest fluctuations.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A change in market prices exposes the Company to market risk related to its investments.&#160;&#160;As of December 29, 2012, all investments were classified as available-for-sale securities and totaled $1,759,000.&#160;&#160;A hypothetical 10% drop in the market value of these investments would result in a $176,000 unrealized loss and a corresponding decrease in the fair value of these instruments.&#160;&#160;This hypothetical drop would not affect cash flow and would not have an impact on earnings until the Company sold the investments.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has employed what it believes to be a conservative investment strategy.&#160;&#160;The Company chooses what it believes are low risk investments with high credit, quality institutions.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Item 13.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Certain Relationships, Related Transactions and Director Independence</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The management of the Company is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States.&#160;&#160;Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&#160;&#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s management assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 29, 2012.&#160;&#160;In making the assessment, it used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Internal Control - Integrated Framework</font>.&#160;&#160;Based on that assessment, management concluded that, as of December 29, 2012, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is effective based on those criteria.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Arden Group, Inc. and Consolidated Subsidiaries (the Company) as of December 29, 2012 and December 31, 2011, and the related consolidated statements of comprehensive income, stockholders&#8217; equity and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 29, 2012.&#160;&#160;We also have audited the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 29, 2012, based on criteria established in<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> Internal Control - Integrated Framework</font> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for these financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting.&#160;&#160;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements and an opinion on the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audits.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160;&#160;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&#160;&#160;Our audits of the consolidated financial statements included examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall consolidated financial statement presentation.&#160;&#160;Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk.&#160;&#160;Our audits also include performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&#160;&#160;We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160;&#160;A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></div>

<div align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ARDEN GROUP, INC. AND CONSOLIDATED SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">_______________________________________________________</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 30pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Basis of Presentation and Business Description</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The consolidated financial statements of Arden Group, Inc. (Company or Arden) include the accounts of the Company and its direct and indirect subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Arden is a holding company which conducts operations through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Arden-Mayfair, Inc. (Arden-Mayfair) and Arden-Mayfair&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiary, Gelson&#8217;s Markets (Gelson&#8217;s) which operates 17 supermarkets in Southern California.&#160;&#160;The Company and Arden-Mayfair also own certain real estate properties through a wholly-owned subsidiary, Mayfair Realty, Inc.&#160;&#160;All intercompany accounts and transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Fiscal Year</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company operates on a fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to December 31.&#160;&#160;Fiscal years for the consolidated financial statements included herein ended on December 29, 2012 (fiscal 2012 - 52 weeks), December 31, 2011 (fiscal 2011 - 52 weeks) and January 1, 2011 (fiscal 2010 - 52 weeks).</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;The following is a summary of significant accounting policies followed in the preparation of these consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">&#160;<font style="TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Reclassifications</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">&#160;Certain amounts in prior periods have been reclassified to conform to the current period financial statement presentation.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows classify changes in cash and cash equivalents (short-term, highly liquid investments with maturity of three months or less at the date of purchase) according to operating, investing or financing activities.&#160;&#160;The Company places its temporary cash investments with what it believes to be high credit, quality financial institutions.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Investments</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company invests in marketable securities including U.S. Treasuries, certificates of deposit, money market funds, commercial paper, mutual funds and corporate and government securities.&#160;&#160;Marketable securities are stated at market value as determined by the most recently traded price of each security at the balance sheet date.&#160;&#160;The Company reviews its investment portfolio on a quarterly basis to determine if market declines below book value may be other-than-temporary.&#160;&#160;Any decline that is determined to be other-than-temporary is recorded as a loss on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income in accordance with authoritative guidance.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management determines the appropriate classification of its investments in marketable securities at the time of purchase and reevaluates such determination at each balance sheet date.&#160;&#160;Debt securities that the Company does not intend to hold to maturity and equity securities are classified as available-for-sale.&#160;&#160;As of December 29, 2012, all marketable securities were classified as available-for-sale.&#160;&#160;Investments are carried at fair value, with the unrealized gains and losses, net of tax, reported as a separate component of stockholders&#8217; equity.&#160;&#160;The cost of investments sold is determined based on the Specific Identification method.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Accounts Receivable</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company monitors Gelson&#8217;s charge card and vendor receivables on an ongoing basis and has not experienced significant losses related to its receivables.&#160;&#160;At December 29, 2012, the Company believes that it did not have significant credit risk concentrations.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Inventories</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Supermarket nonperishable inventories are recorded using the retail method and are stated at the lower of cost or market, with cost determined using the last-in, first-out (LIFO) method.&#160;&#160;Perishable inventories are valued at the lower of cost on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis or market.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Inventory reserves are maintained for dry goods at historical run rates that are adjusted annually and trued up at each physical count (three times per year) to ensure adequacy of the reserve.&#160;&#160;Inventories of perishable items are taken at the end of every month and balances are adjusted accordingly with the offset recorded in cost of sales.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Leased property meeting certain capital lease criteria is capitalized and the present value of the related lease payments is recorded as a liability.&#160;&#160;Amortization of capitalized leased assets is computed on the straight-line method over the shorter of the estimated useful life or the initial lease term.&#160;&#160;There were no capitalized leases at December 29, 2012 and December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Normal repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred.&#160;&#160;Expenditures which materially increase values, change capacities or extend useful lives are capitalized.&#160;&#160;Replacements are capitalized and the property, plant and equipment accounts are relieved of the items being replaced.&#160;&#160;The related costs and accumulated depreciation of disposed assets are eliminated and any gain or loss on disposition is included in selling, general and administrative (SG&amp;A) expense on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 30pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company monitors the carrying value of long-lived assets for potential impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of an asset may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;Impairment is recognized when estimated future cash flows (undiscounted and before interest charges) are less than carrying value.&#160;&#160;The estimation of expected future net cash flows is inherently uncertain and relies on assumptions regarding current and future economic and market conditions and the availability of capital.&#160;&#160;If impairment analysis assumptions change, then an adjustment to the carrying value of the Company&#8217;s long-lived assets could occur.&#160;&#160;To the extent that an asset is impaired, the excess of the carrying amount of the asset over its estimated fair value is charged against earnings.&#160;&#160;No impairments were recorded in 2012, 2011 or 2010.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Workers&#8217; Compensation and General and Auto Liability Costs</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is primarily self-insured through the use of a high deductible policy for losses related to workers&#8217; compensation for claims incurred prior to July 1, 2006, as well as all general and auto liability claims.&#160;&#160;The Company maintains stop-loss coverage to limit its loss exposure on a per claim basis and is insured for covered costs in excess of per claim limits.&#160;&#160;Since July 1, 2006, the Company has purchased fully insured guaranteed cost workers&#8217; compensation insurance to replace the high deductible program.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>The Company continues to maintain an accrual for workers&#8217; compensation claims incurred prior to July 2006 under the high deductible program which is based on undeveloped reported claims and an estimate of claims incurred but not reported.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s workers&#8217; compensation and general and auto liability reserves for unpaid and incurred but not reported claims at December 29, 2012 and December 31, 2011 were approximately $1,967,000 and $3,006,000, respectively.&#160;&#160;While the ultimate amount of claims incurred are dependent on future developments, the recorded reserves reflect management&#8217;s best estimate of claims to be incurred.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Revenue Recognition</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company recognizes revenue at the time of sale.&#160;&#160;Discounts given to customers are recorded at the point of sale as a reduction of revenues.&#160;&#160;The Company maintains a bad debt allowance for receivables from vendors and Gelson&#8217;s charge card users.&#160;&#160;Valuation reserves are adjusted periodically based on historical recovery rates.&#160;&#160;The Company records income from licensing arrangements, subleases, leases and finance charges as they are earned.&#160;&#160;Income from all licensing arrangements, rental income and finance charges represents approximately 1% or less of sales for all periods presented and, therefore, is not disclosed separately on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gelson&#8217;s sells gift cards to its customers in its retail stores.&#160;&#160;The gift cards do not have an expiration date and Gelson&#8217;s does not charge an administrative fee on unused gift cards.&#160;&#160;The Company records unredeemed gift cards in Accounts Payable, Trade on its Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The Company recognizes revenue when the gift cards are redeemed or when the likelihood of the gift cards being redeemed is remote and there is no legal obligation to remit the unredeemed gift cards to relevant jurisdictions (gift card breakage).&#160;&#160;Based on an analysis of historical redemption patterns, the Company determined the appropriate gift card breakage rate is three years.&#160;&#160;During 2012, 2011 and 2010, the Company recorded $40,000, $52,000 and $43,000 of revenue related to gift card breakage, respectively.&#160;&#160;Gift card breakage is included in Sales on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Cost of Sales</font></font></div>

<td valign="bottom" width="12%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">34,388</font></font></td>
<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></td>

<td valign="bottom" width="12%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">33,928</font></font></font></td>
<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></td>

<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Fair Value Measurements</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair value is defined as the amount that would be received upon sale of an asset or paid to transfer a liability in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.&#160;&#160;The authoritative guidance establishes a fair value hierarchy which prioritizes the types of inputs to valuation techniques that companies may use to measure fair value.&#160;&#160;The fair value hierarchy gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1).&#160;&#160;The next highest priority is given to inputs other than quoted prices included in Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly (Level 2).&#160;&#160;The lowest priority is given to unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data available and which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions (Level 3).&#160;&#160;The fair value of the Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities measured on a recurring basis includes investments which appear under Assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;See Note 2 for a disaggregation of the Company&#8217;s investments including the input level used to determine fair value for each type of investment.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The carrying values of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, accounts payable and accrued liabilities approximate fair value because of the short-term maturity of these instruments.&#160;&#160;The fair value of the Company&#8217;s long-term debt closely approximates its carrying value.&#160;&#160;The Company estimates the fair value of long-term debt based upon the net present value of the future cash flows using those interest rates that are currently available to the Company for the issuance of debt with similar terms and remaining maturities.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Vendor Allowances</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company receives a variety of allowances from its vendors whose products are sold in Gelson&#8217;s stores.&#160;&#160;Typically, the vendors are paying the Company to promote their products.&#160;&#160;The promotion may be a temporary price reduction, a feature in a print advertisement or newsletter, placement of the vendor&#8217;s product in a preferred location in a store or introduction of a new product.&#160;&#160;The promotions range from approximately two weeks to six months and are recognized as a reduction of cost of sales as they are earned.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Occasionally, the Company receives rebate allowances in the form of upfront lump-sum payments from vendors.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of these long-term agreements (which typically extend for several months or years), the Company earns the rebates as it purchases product from the vendor.&#160;&#160;The upfront payments are recorded as a liability when they are received and are recorded as a reduction of inventory cost as the product is purchased.&#160;&#160;In the event the Company does not purchase the minimum amount of product specified in the agreement, the upfront payments must be returned on a pro rata basis to the vendor.&#160;&#160;If the contract does not specify that the rebate is earned as product is purchased, then the upfront payments are recorded as a liability when received and recognized as a reduction of cost of sales on a pro rata basis as the product is sold.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Stock Appreciation Rights</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has outstanding stock appreciation rights (SARs) that have been granted to non-employee directors and certain employees.&#160;&#160;Each SAR entitles the holder to receive cash upon exercise equal to the excess of the fair market value of a share of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock (Class A), as determined in accordance with the SARs agreement, on the date of exercise over the fair market value of such share on the date granted.&#160;&#160;All currently outstanding&#160;&#160;&#160;SARs vest 25% each year beginning at the end of the third year and expire seven years from the date of grant.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair value of each SAR is estimated at the end of each reporting period using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.&#160;&#160;The Black-Scholes option-pricing model incorporates various highly subjective assumptions, including expected term, expected volatility, expected dividend yield and a risk-free interest rate.&#160;&#160;The Company has reviewed its historical pattern of SARs exercises and has determined that meaningful differences in SARs exercise activity exist between employees and non-employee directors.&#160;&#160;Consequently, the Company has categorized SARs into two groups for valuation purposes, as well as separate groups based on grant date.&#160;&#160;Expected volatility was determined based on<font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #ff0000">&#160;</font>historical volatility using weekly data.&#160;&#160;The risk-free interest rate is based on U.S. Treasury zero-coupon issues with a remaining term equal to the expected SARs life assumed at the date of grant less the time that has elapsed since the grant date.&#160;&#160;The expected term was calculated based on historical experience.&#160;&#160;Authoritative guidance also requires that a forfeiture assumption be applied to awards that are classified as liabilities such as SARs.&#160;&#160;However, cash-settled SARs are remeasured at fair value at the end of each reporting period and, therefore, the impact of actual forfeitures will be reflected at each remeasurement date.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Rental Expense and Income</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Rental payments on operating leases are recorded over the lease term as they become payable or receivable except for rental payments on leases with scheduled rent increases which are recognized on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Income Taxes</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the difference between the financial statement and tax bases of assets and liabilities, using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.&#160;&#160;The realization of deferred tax assets is contingent upon the Company&#8217;s ability to generate future taxable income.&#160;&#160;See Note 13 for further information.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Common Stock and Net Income Per Share</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Basic net income per common share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&#160;&#160;Diluted net income per common share is determined by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common and potential common shares outstanding during the period.&#160;&#160;There were no potential common shares outstanding during the periods presented and, therefore, basic and diluted net income per common share are the same.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Use of Estimates</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP) requires management to make estimates and assumptions for the reporting period and as of the financial statement date.&#160;&#160;These estimates and assumptions affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, the disclosure of contingent liabilities and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from these estimates.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 30pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Impact of Recently Issued Accounting Standards</font></font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In May 2011, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) 2011-04, &#8220;Amendments to Achieve Common Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure Requirements in U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).&#8221;&#160;&#160;This pronouncement was issued to provide a consistent definition of fair value and ensure that the fair value measurement and disclosure requirements are similar between U.S. GAAP and IFRS.&#160;&#160;ASU 2011-04 changes certain fair value measurement principles and enhances the disclosure requirements particularly for level three fair value measurements.&#160;&#160;This pronouncement is effective for reporting periods beginning on or after December 15, 2011.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASU 2011-04 did not have any impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position or results of operations.</font></div>
<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2013, the FASB issued ASU 2013-02, &#8220;Reporting of Amounts Reclassified Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income.&#8221;&#160;&#160;This amendment does not change the current requirements for reporting net income or other comprehensive income in financial statements; however, the amendment requires an entity to provide information about the amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by component and to disclose significant amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by the respective line items of net income if the amount being reclassified is required under U.S.&#160;GAAP to be reclassified in its entirety to net income.&#160;&#160;For other amounts that are not required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in their entirety to net income in the same reporting period, an entity is required to cross-reference other disclosures required under U.S. GAAP.&#160;&#160;The pronouncement is effective for reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2012.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASU 2013-02 is not expected to have a significant impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Significant Supplier</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2012, the Company procured approximately 14% of its product through Unified Grocers, Inc. (Unified), a grocery wholesale cooperative.&#160;&#160;As a member-patron, the Company is required to provide Unified with certain minimum deposits in order to purchase product from the cooperative.&#160;&#160;As of December 29, 2012, the Company had approximately $1,360,000 on deposit with Unified in addition to approximately $694,000 related to ownership of equity shares in Unified.&#160;&#160;There is no established public trading market for Unified&#8217;s shares.&#160;&#160;The deposit and equity ownership are recorded in other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unified pays dividends annually in December of each year.&#160;&#160;Dividends are paid in arrears and are based on a percentage of the Company&#8217;s qualifying purchases from Unified, which percentage is typically established by Unified at or after the end of each year.&#160;&#160;The Company accrues patronage dividend income as a reduction of cost of sales ratably throughout the year based on a review of prior dividend history, projected purchase volume and an estimate of Unified&#8217;s current year patronage earnings.&#160;&#160;The accrual is adjusted each year, as needed, based on the actual amount received from Unified in December.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 30pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has an unsecured revolving line of credit facility available for standby letters of credit, funding operations and expansion.&#160;&#160;The credit agreement provides for borrowings and/or letters of credit up to an aggregate principal amount at any one time of $25,000,000 and expires on June 1, 2014.&#160;&#160;Borrowings bear interest at the adjusted London Interbank Offer Rate (LIBOR) plus a margin or at the bank&#8217;s prime rate minus a margin.&#160;&#160;In either case, the margin is dependent upon the Company&#8217;s Leverage Ratio as defined in the credit agreement.&#160;&#160;At the end of 2012, there were no amounts borrowed against the line of credit.&#160;&#160;The Company currently maintains four standby letters of credit aggregating $7,644,000 in connection with lease and self-insurance requirements.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 32pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Debentures: The indenture relating to the 7% Subordinated Income Debentures (7% Debentures), due September 1, 2014, provides for interest payable semi-annually on March&#160;1 and September 1 to the extent that current annual net income is sufficient therefor, or at the discretion of the Company, out of available retained earnings.&#160;&#160;All interest due and payable as of December 29, 2012 was paid.&#160;&#160;The 7% Debentures are recorded at face value which approximates its fair value.</font></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">9.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Capital Stock</font></div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 32pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is authorized to issue 10,000,000 shares of Class A, par value $0.25 per share.&#160;&#160;At December 29, 2012 and December 31, 2011, the number of shares issued were 4,428,200 including 1,357,200 treasury shares.&#160;&#160;The Company has a stock repurchase program, authorized by the Board of Directors, to purchase shares of its Class A in the open market or in private transactions from time to time.&#160;&#160;The timing, volume and price of purchases are at the discretion of the management of the Company.&#160;&#160;In April 2011, the Company purchased and retired 90,098 shares of its Class A for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $6,684,000 in an unsolicited private transaction.&#160;&#160;After taking into account this purchase and purchases in prior years, up to 132,806 shares of Class A remain authorized for repurchase.&#160;&#160;No stock was repurchased under this program in 2012 or 2010.</font></div></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 32pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2012, 2011 and 2010, the Company paid regular quarterly dividends of $0.25 per share of Class A for a total of approximately $3,071,000, $3,116,000 and $3,161,000, respectively.&#160;&#160;On November 20, 2012, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors declared a special cash dividend of twenty dollars ($20) per share on its outstanding Class A payable on December 18, 2012 to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 3, 2012.&#160;&#160;The aggregate amount of the special cash&#160;dividend was approximately $61,420,000.&#160;&#160;The Board of Directors also approved a $20 antidilution adjustment reducing the exercise price of all outstanding SARs issued prior to November 20, 2012 to account for the anticipated effect of the special cash&#160;dividend on the Company&#8217;s Class A share price.&#160;&#160;On January 18, 2013, the Company paid a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share of Class A, aggregating approximately $768,000, to stockholders of record on December 28, 2012.</font></div></div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">10.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock Appreciation Rights</font></div>
</div>

<div style="LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 32pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has granted SARs covering shares of the Company&#8217;s Class A to non-employee directors and certain employees of the Company and its subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Each SAR entitles the holder to receive upon exercise thereof the excess of the fair market value of a share of Class&#160;A, as determined in accordance with the SARs agreement, on the date of exercise over the fair market value of such share on the date granted.&#160;&#160;All currently outstanding SARs vest 25% each year beginning at the end of the third year and expire seven years from the date of grant.&#160;&#160;SARs transactions during the past three years are summarized below.</font></div>
